## Appendix C: Detailed search results {.unnumbered}

These comparisons support the highlights in the main Results. Results at ≥0.02 retain the original response, and results at >0.04 are the separate management assessment. Comparisons summarised in a sentence here have their full tables in `outputs/tables/`.

### Habitat layers {.unnumbered}

![The three main habitat layers across the Great Barrier Reef, shown as cell means at about 2.9 km. The two cull-trained layers (left, centre) are annual probabilities of a problematic cull site-year in 2026; the HMSC layer (right) is conditional on an active reef-year. Gaps in RG + year are reefs without ReefGuide layers, filled by the clean + year fallback in the primary search-planning layer.](../outputs/figures/fig01_gbr_overview.png){#fig-overview width="100%"}

Imagery attribution for the map figures: Tiles © Esri — Source: Esri, i-cubed, USDA, USGS, AEX, GeoEye, Getmapping, Aerogrid, IGN, IGP, UPR-EGP, and the GIS User Community.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-manta
#| tbl-cap: "Discrimination between strong-evidence and strictly negative manta tows within reef-years. Manta tows were not used to fit any of these layers. Lift is the share of strong-evidence tows in a reef-year's top 20% of tows, divided by 20%. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years."
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Layer = mic$layer,
  `Within reef-year AUC (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a3(mic$within_reef_year_auc), a3(mic$auc_low), a3(mic$auc_high)),
  `Top-20% lift (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a2(mic$top20_lift), a2(mic$lift_low), a2(mic$lift_high)),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lll")
```

The layers agree only in part on which cells rank highest. Median within-reef Spearman correlations were `r a2(pick(la, pair = "Clean + year vs RG + year", col = "median"))` between clean + year and RG + year, `r a2(pick(la, pair = "Clean + year vs HMSC joint", col = "median"))` between clean + year and HMSC, and `r a2(pick(la, pair = "RG + year vs HMSC joint", col = "median"))` between RG + year and HMSC. Where both cull-trained layers exist, the fallback and RG rankings correlate at `r a2(fbc$spearman)`, so ranks near the RG coverage boundary within a reef are less reliable.

Used alone to rank all designated sites on a reef, the held-out habitat layer retained problematic dives only slightly faster than low-density or ghost dives. Searching the top 70% of sites retained `r cip(cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7), cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7, col = "low"), cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7, col = "high"))` of problematic dives. A ranking with no information would have retained `r p1(cs("dives_kept", 0.7))`. Within reef-years, the AUC was `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "leave-reef-out", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` for problematic versus low-density dives and `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "leave-reef-out", col = "auc_problematic_vs_ghost"))` versus ghost dives. The in-sample layer looked stronger (`r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "deployed", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` and `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "deployed", col = "auc_problematic_vs_ghost"))`) only because it had been trained on those dives.

### Recent evidence and cull-site selection {.unnumbered}

In the original ≥0.02 evaluation, adding last season's cull dives and manta tows to habitat reduced the search needed for the same problematic dives (@tbl-evidence). Held out over 2018–2026 (`r int(ev_dives)` dives in `r int(ev_ry)` reef-years), with 90% of problematic dives retained, designated sites searched fell from `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.9, "habitat"))` to `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.9, "combined"))`, and all paired intervals excluded zero. Most of the reduction came from ranking quiet and never-dived sites lower: among dives actually made, discrimination between problematic and low-density dives rose only from `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "all", score = "habitat", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` to `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "all", score = "combined", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`. In the fitted model, strong manta tows or problematic dives nearby raised a site's rank, and a site dived the previous season with nothing problematic dropped sharply.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Habitat-only ranking → habitat plus previous-season evidence, compared at matched retention of problematic dives (CPUE ≥0.02; held out). Brackets: 95% paired bootstrap interval of the difference, in percentage points."
cell <- function(metric, r, period) sprintf("%s → %s (%s)", p0(ev(metric, r, "habitat", period)), p0(ev(metric, r, "combined", period)),
  gpp(ev(metric, r, "combined", period, "gain_low"), ev(metric, r, "combined", period, "gain_high")))
rows <- expand.grid(r = c(0.9, 0.8), period = c("2018-2026", "2022-2026"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Period = sub("-", "–", rows$period),
  `Problematic dives kept` = p0(rows$r),
  `Designated sites searched` = mapply(cell, "sites_searched", rows$r, rows$period),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = mapply(cell, "low_dives_avoided", rows$r, rows$period),
  `Ghost dives avoided` = mapply(cell, "ghost_dives_avoided", rows$r, rows$period),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

The evidence model was also tested using earlier seasons to predict later ones. Its habitat models were withheld by reef but were not restricted to earlier years. It avoided more low-density dives than habitat alone in every season from 2022, and searched fewer sites in every season from 2023 (@tbl-seasons). It did not help in 2019–2021, when fewer earlier seasons were available to learn from.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-seasons
#| tbl-cap: "Year-by-year forward test of the cull-site ranking with 90% of problematic dives (CPUE ≥0.02) retained. Each season uses an evidence model fitted only on earlier seasons, with habitat models withheld by reef. Values are habitat alone → cull-trained habitat + last season's evidence (all earlier seasons)."
periods <- c(as.character(2019:2026), "2019-2026")
lab <- c(as.character(2019:2025), "2026 (Jan–May)", "2019–2026")
arrow <- function(p, metric, f = p0) sprintf("%s → %s", f(fw("habitat_only", metric, p)), f(fw("cull_all", metric, p)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Test season` = lab,
  Dives = vapply(periods, function(p) int(fw("cull_all", "sites_searched_at_90", p, "dives")), ""),
  `Cull sites selected` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "sites_searched_at_90"),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "low_dives_avoided_at_90"),
  `AUC, problematic vs low-density` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "auc_problematic_vs_low", f = a2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrlll")
```

A caveat applies to all cull-site results. A ranking is credited when it agrees with where crews chose to dive. Crews already use the previous season's knowledge, so part of the gain formalises current practice. COTS densities at designated sites that were never dived cannot be verified from these data.

### Retention of dives above 0.04 CPUE and tow effort {.unnumbered}

The acceptable loss makes a large difference (@tbl-search-highlights, @fig-high-density). Retaining 99% of >0.04 dives required `r hdci("sites_searched", 0.99)` of site-years with the combined ranking, leaving much less scope to avoid low-density and ghost dives. The proposed 10–15% search reduction therefore cannot be assumed compatible with negligible omissions; the allowed omission rate must be agreed and tested in the field.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-search-highlights
#| tbl-cap: "Cull sites selected for dives and low-density or ghost dives avoided, 2019–2026. Upper rows fix retention of >0.04 CPUE dives; final rows fix the A–D site count and report retention. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals]. Sites are candidate site-years, including never-dived sites, rather than confirmed culling visits. Low-density means positive CPUE <0.02; ghost means zero; intermediate dives (0.02–0.04 inclusive) are separate. Appendix B gives validation details; @tbl-manta-effort gives manta effort. Annual follow-up is excluded."
highlight_rows <- expand.grid(target = c(0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99), score = c("habitat", "combined", "random"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
highlight_rows <- highlight_rows[order(highlight_rows$target, highlight_rows$score), ]
highlight_metric <- function(metric) vapply(seq_len(nrow(highlight_rows)), function(i) {
  x <- highlight_rows[i, ]
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score),
    100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, col = "low"), 100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, col = "high"))
}, character(1))
highlight_table <- data.frame(
  `High-density retained (%)` = as.character(100 * highlight_rows$target),
  Ranking = c(combined = "Habitat + recent observations", habitat = "Habitat alone", random = "Random selection")[highlight_rows$score],
  `Sites selected for cull dives (%)` = highlight_metric("sites_searched"),
  `Low-density avoided (%)` = highlight_metric("low_avoided"),
  `Ghost dives avoided (%)` = highlight_metric("ghost_avoided"),
  check.names = FALSE)
opsc <- c("combined", "habitat", "random")
opcell <- function(metric) vapply(opsc, function(s) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * oc(metric, s), 100 * oc(metric, s, "low"), 100 * oc(metric, s, "high")), "")
operational_rows <- data.frame(opcell("high_retained"),
  c("A–D: habitat + recent observations", "A–D count: habitat alone", "A–D count: random selection"),
  opcell("sites_selected"), opcell("low_avoided"), opcell("ghost_avoided"), check.names = FALSE)
names(operational_rows) <- names(highlight_table)
knitr::kable(rbind(highlight_table, operational_rows), row.names = FALSE)
```

![Retention of observed dives above 0.04 CPUE against cull site-years selected for dives, using the existing forward evidence rankings. Random selection has the same site count on each reef. Shading shows 95% reef-year bootstrap intervals; dotted horizontal lines mark 80%, 90%, 95% and 99% retention. The diamond marks the exact A–D cutoff used for the priority classes in @fig-2027 and the final rows of @tbl-search-highlights. Habitat fits were held out by reef, while the evidence regression used earlier seasons. Follow-up surveys were not evaluated.](../outputs/figures/fig20_high_density_retention.png){#fig-high-density width=100%}

At the A–D cutoff the ranking deferred `r odci("all_dives_avoided")` of recorded dives, compared with `r odci("all_dives_avoided", "random")` under random site selection, because it retained more repeatedly visited sites. It retained `r odci("intermediate_retained")` of dives from 0.02 to 0.04. Of its `r int(sum(opbreakdown$deferred_dives))` deferred dives, `r p1(od("quiet_share_deferred"))` were ghost or low-density, compared with `r p1(od("quiet_share_deferred", "random"))` under random selection. Equal candidate-site counts did not represent equal dive effort (@tbl-operational-highlights).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-operational-highlights
#| tbl-cap: "The site rule (retain classes A–D, defer E) and the workflow under within-reef classes, 2019–2026. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals]. Site-rule columns: both rankings select the same candidate-site count, not the same recorded dive count; tow rows are conditional spatial estimates before annual checks and exploration. Workflow columns: dives on 1,876 reef visits with a manta survey, ranked at voyage departure; open-site and strong-evidence dives are kept and only the other dives are ranked (A–C retained); the random column skips the same number of those dives at random. Workflow dive rows use the dive rule alone; the workflow tow row is tows skipped by the follow-up zone with season memory, as a share of all tows made, and Appendix D combines the two. Upper rows use all sites, dives or dives in the stated CPUE class as their denominator; lower rows describe deferred dives and sum to 100% in each column. The density-aware results are in Appendix D."
op_metrics <- c("sites_selected","all_dives_avoided","high_retained","intermediate_retained","low_avoided","ghost_avoided","manta_tows_avoided","manta_distance_avoided",
 "share_deferred_ghost","share_deferred_low","share_deferred_intermediate","share_deferred_high")
op_labels <- c("Candidate cull sites selected","All recorded dives avoided","Dives above 0.04 CPUE retained","Dives at 0.02–0.04 CPUE retained","Low-density dives avoided (0 < CPUE <0.02)","Ghost dives avoided (CPUE = 0)","Whole manta tows potentially avoided","Manta distance potentially avoided",
 "Ghost: CPUE = 0","Low: 0 < CPUE <0.02","Intermediate: 0.02 ≤ CPUE ≤0.04","High: CPUE >0.04")
op_value <- function(m,score,col) if(m %in% opcut$metric) oc(m,score,col) else od(m,score,col)
op_format <- function(score) vapply(op_metrics, function(m) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]",100*op_value(m,score,"value"),100*op_value(m,score,"low"),100*op_value(m,score,"high")),"")
wf_map <- c(sites_selected=NA,all_dives_avoided="dives_avoided_pct",high_retained="high_missed_pct",intermediate_retained="inter_missed_pct",
 low_avoided="low_avoided_pct",ghost_avoided="ghost_avoided_pct",manta_tows_avoided="tows_saved_pct",manta_distance_avoided=NA,
 share_deferred_ghost="share_deferred_ghost",share_deferred_low="share_deferred_low",share_deferred_intermediate="share_deferred_intermediate",
 share_deferred_high="share_deferred_high")
wf_format <- function(variant) vapply(op_metrics, function(m) {
  k <- wf_map[[m]]
  if (is.na(k) || (variant == RWF && k == "tows_saved_pct")) return("—")
  v <- if (variant == WF && k == "tows_saved_pct") WFZ else variant
  x <- c(ps(v, k), ps(v, k, "low"), ps(v, k, "high"))
  if (m %in% c("high_retained", "intermediate_retained")) x <- 1 - x[c(1, 3, 2)]
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * x[1], 100 * x[2], 100 * x[3])
}, "")
op_rows <- data.frame(Outcome=op_labels,`Site rule: habitat + recent observations`=op_format("combined"),`Site rule: random sites`=op_format("random"),
 `Workflow: A–C for dives without strong evidence`=wf_format(WF),`Workflow: same dives at random`=wf_format(RWF),check.names=FALSE)
op_rows <- rbind(op_rows[1:8,],setNames(data.frame("**Composition of deferred dives**","","","",""),names(op_rows)),op_rows[9:12,])
knitr::kable(op_rows,row.names=FALSE)
```

At the same cutoff, `r occi("manta_tows_avoided")` of recorded tows lay entirely within deferred-only sites, and `r occi("manta_distance_avoided")` of straight-line tow distance lay within those sites. Both estimates keep surveillance outside designated sites and in any overlap with retained sites, and neither establishes detection after removing that surveillance.

The spatial effort estimate (@tbl-manta-effort) used `r int(opcover$manta_valid_segments)` valid tow segments from `r int(opcover$manta_reef_years)` of the `r int(opcover$reef_years)` evaluated reef-years. Designated sites contained `r p1(opcover$distance_inside_sites)` of the valid distance, and surveillance outside that footprint remains in the calculation at every cutoff.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-manta-effort
#| tbl-cap: "Potential manta-surveillance reductions paired with @tbl-search-highlights, before annual checks or exploration. Upper rows use the stated dive-retention targets; final rows fix the A–D site count. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals] refer to whole recorded tows or total straight-line segment distance. Surveillance outside designated sites and in overlaps with retained sites remains. These spatial effort proxies assume retained cull visits still occur; detection after tow removal, route feasibility and time savings are untested."
manta_rows <- data.frame(Rule = paste0(c(80,90,95,99), "% dive retention"),
  Ranking = "Habitat + recent observations", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for(metric in c("manta_tows_avoided", "manta_distance_avoided")) {
  vals <- vapply(c(.8,.9,.95,.99), function(t) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * om(metric,t), 100 * om(metric,t,col="low"), 100 * om(metric,t,col="high")), "")
  manta_rows[[metric]] <- vals
}
manta_op <- data.frame(Rule = "A–D site count", Ranking = c("Habitat + recent observations", "Habitat alone", "Random selection"),
  manta_tows_avoided = opcell("manta_tows_avoided"), manta_distance_avoided = opcell("manta_distance_avoided"))
manta_table <- rbind(manta_rows, manta_op)
names(manta_table)[3:4] <- c("Whole manta tows avoided (%)", "Manta tow distance avoided (%)")
knitr::kable(manta_table, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Cull history and reefs without recent evidence {.unnumbered}

Problematic sites persist between seasons at a scale of about 0.5–1 km. In the strictly forward test, the blend of habitat and cull history reached a within reef-year AUC of `r ci3(fvh("combined_fixed"), fvh("combined_fixed", col = "auc_low"), fvh("combined_fixed", col = "auc_high"))`, against `r a3(fvh("habitat"))` for habitat alone (@tbl-forward). It reached `r a3(fvh("combined_fixed", "with nearby history"))` with history nearby and `r a3(fvh("combined_fixed", "new sites"))` at sites never culled before. Part of the skill reflects operator behaviour: a score based only on how often crews had dived a site reached `r a3(fvh("effort"))`. This layer is therefore delivered as a map of **known aggregation sites** for briefing crews, not as habitat.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-forward
#| tbl-cap: "Forward validation: within reef-year AUC for problematic cull site-years, test years 2022–2026 pooled. Each score uses only data from before the test year. The deployed blend's 95% bootstrap interval over reef-years is given for all site-years."
meth <- c(habitat = "Habitat (HMSC refitted before test year)", habitat_context = "Habitat + reef context",
          effort = "Dive effort only", history_fixed = "History kernel", combined_fixed = "Habitat + history (deployed)")
subs <- c("all", "with nearby history", "little or no nearby history", "new sites")
tf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(meth), function(m) {
  v <- vapply(subs, function(s) a3(fvh(m, s)), "")
  v[1] <- if (m == "combined_fixed") ci3(fvh(m), fvh(m, col = "auc_low"), fvh(m, col = "auc_high")) else v[1]
  data.frame(Score = meth[[m]], t(v), check.names = FALSE)
}))
names(tf)[-1] <- sprintf("%s (n = %s)", c("All site-years", "With nearby history", "Little or none", "New sites"),
                         vapply(subs, function(s) int(fvh("habitat", s, col = "site_years")), ""))
knitr::kable(tf, row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

Recent evidence is unevenly spread. `r p0(1 - pick(ecov, window = "last_season", col = "share_reef_any_prev"))` of reef-years were on reefs not visited the season before. On those reefs (`r int(nv_dives)` dives) every ranking was close to chance (AUC about `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "reef not visited", score = "combined", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`), and habitat was the only information available.

Habitat also reaches ground that recent search has not covered. A tow was counted as *new ground* if no tow lay within 300 m in the previous five seasons. On new ground, the manta model ranked tows with a within reef-year AUC of `r ci3(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "value"), pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "low"), pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "high"))`, and the cull-trained layer at `r a2(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "value"))`. Strong evidence was more common on new ground than on repeat ground (`r p1(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "strong_share"))` vs `r p1(pick(eng, ground = "repeat ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "strong_share"))` of tows), partly because new ground is often surveyed early in an irruption. This is the basis for the exploration zones in the 2027 product.

### Manta surveillance {.unnumbered}

Systematic thinning found the most aggregations at every level of effort (@tbl-thinning, @fig-aggregations-detail). The largest cut that still found at least 95% of aggregations was `r p0(mx("systematic_point"))` of tows for systematic thinning (`r p0(mx("systematic_assured"))` with bootstrap assurance), `r p0(mx("random_point"))` for random thinning and `r p0(mx("layer_cv_point"))` for thinning by habitat rank. Ranking concentrates the kept tows in a few high-scoring stretches of reef, so aggregations in low-scoring stretches are missed entirely.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thinning
#| tbl-cap: "Share of COTS aggregations (two or more strong-evidence tows within 500 m) still found when manta tows are cut within each survey, all years. The layer is the cull-trained RG + year model scored leave-reef-out; the deployed column is the same layer scored in-sample. Brackets: 95% bootstrap interval over surveys."
k <- c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Tows kept` = p0(k),
  `Layer, held out` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv")), ""),
                              vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv_low")), ""), vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv_high")), "")),
  `Layer, deployed` = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_deployed")), ""),
  Random = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "random")), ""),
  Systematic = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "systematic")), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lllll")
```

![Manta tows kept versus COTS aggregations found. Left: aggregations of two or more strong-evidence tows found as tows are cut, for the cull-trained layer (held out and deployed), random selection and systematic thinning; bands are 95% bootstrap intervals over surveys. Right: share found at 60% of tows kept, by aggregation size. Evenly spaced thinning loses the fewest aggregations.](../outputs/figures/fig13_manta_aggregation_cv.png){#fig-aggregations-detail width="100%"}

A habitat model trained on manta tows ranked held-out tows best (@tbl-mantamodel), but still found fewer aggregations than random (`r p1(pick(mra, strategy = "random", keep = 0.6, col = "found"))`) or systematic thinning (`r p1(pick(mra, strategy = "systematic", keep = 0.6, col = "found"))`), so its role is to direct extra tows rather than to remove them. Training on manta did not improve cull-site selection: once last season's evidence was added, every habitat model gave the same result.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mantamodel
#| tbl-cap: "Cull-trained and manta-trained habitat models on held-out manta tows (all three fitted on the same leave-reef-out folds). AUC: strong-evidence vs strictly negative tows within reef-years, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Aggregations: share found at 60% of tows kept."
mods <- c(cull = "Cull-trained", manta = "Manta-trained (with year)", within = "Manta-trained, within reef-year")
strat <- c(cull = "cull_cv", manta = "manta_cv", within = "within_cv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Model = unname(mods),
  `Tow AUC (95% CI)` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a3(mt(m, "auc")), a3(mt(m, "auc", "low")), a3(mt(m, "auc", "high"))), ""),
  `Top-20% lift` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) a2(mt(m, "lift")), ""),
  `Aggregations found, 60% kept` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) p1(pick(mra, strategy = strat[[m]], keep = 0.6, col = "found")), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "llll")
```

### The 2027 priority classes {.unnumbered}

Every designated cull site (`r int(n_sites)` sites on `r int(n_reefs)` reefs) was ranked within its reef for the 2027 season, using the combined model with the most recent 12 months of evidence. The ranking is delivered as a CSV and as the EoTR cull-site KMZ, with each polygon coloured by priority class. Each polygon also carries its rank, its modelled chance of a problematic dive if dived, and last season's evidence. @tbl-classes shows what each class kept in the forward test.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-classes
#| tbl-cap: "Original ≥0.02 evaluation: 2027 priority classes and what searching through each class retained in the forward test (dives 2019–2026)."
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Searching through` = c("A", "A + B", "A to C", "A to D", "All (incl. E)"),
  `Sites on the reef` = c("top 20%", "top 50%", "top 66%", "top 80%", "100%"),
  `Problematic dives kept` = p0(cls$problematic_dives_kept),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = p0(cls$low_dives_avoided),
  `Ghost dives avoided` = p0(cls$ghost_dives_avoided),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

- **Evidence ranks the top.** `r int(n_probev)` sites had a problematic dive last season and `r int(n_mantaev)` have strong manta evidence nearby.
- **Evidence also lowers sites.** `r int(n_quiet)` sites were dived last season with nothing problematic, which strongly lowers their rank.
- **Habitat ranks the rest.** `r int(n_noev)` sites (`r p0(n_noev / nrow(pri))`) are on reefs with no dives or tows in the last 12 months. Habitat alone orders them, as a first search order to update once manta tows come in.

The exploration zones add high-ranked habitat outside the current search footprint (@fig-2027), so that the ranking does not keep consolidating search on the same places. The broadest band (top 40% of habitat) covers `r int(nrow(expz_band(0.6, identity)))` reefs, with a median of `r num(expz_band(0.6, function(d) median(d$area_ha)), 0)` ha per reef; the top-10% band covers `r int(nrow(expz_band(0.9, identity)))` reefs, with a median of `r num(expz_band(0.9, function(d) median(d$area_ha)), 0)` ha. On well-surveyed reefs such as Batt and Eyrie, cull sites and five seasons of tows already cover much of the high-ranked habitat, and the zones lie mostly on the reef flat and back reef. The larger opportunities are on reefs with little recent towing. A crew can tow across the darkest band on a visit and record nil results as well as finds.

### Three alternatives to the cull-site ranking {.unnumbered #sec-ranking-alternatives}

Three alternatives were specified before fitting. The first replaced the direct-site indicator of any preceding-season dive at ≥0.02 with any dive strictly above 0.04. The second added a recency-weighted site CPUE (90-day half-life) and its effective number of recent dives. The third used the same recent evidence but replaced mean habitat with the 90th percentile of predictions within the site. All three still learned the ≥0.02 response, with coefficients refitted only on years preceding each test year, and were scored on the same `r int(rscope("evaluated_dives"))` dives. A separate control refitted the original model using the all-cell mean of habitat.

At matched 90% high-density retention, recent CPUE avoided `r rkci("dives_avoided")` of recorded dives, versus `r rkci("dives_avoided","archived")` with the incumbent (@tbl-ranking-candidate-matched). Its paired gain was `r rdci("dives_avoided")` percentage points, and the interval included zero. When recorded-dive coverage was matched to the incumbent's A–D budget, recent CPUE retained `r rkci("high_retained",rule="matched_dives",target=.8)` of high-density dives versus `r rkci("high_retained","archived","matched_dives",.8)`; that paired gain, `r rdci("high_retained",rule="matched_dives",target=.8)` percentage points, also remained uncertain.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ranking-candidate-matched
#| tbl-cap: "Candidate rankings at 90% retention of >0.04 dives, 2019–2026. Percentages [95% intervals]; differences are percentage points [paired 95% intervals] relative to the incumbent. This comparison uses integer site counts at 1% cutoff steps and first-crossing interpolation, so incumbent values can differ slightly from @tbl-search-highlights. The all-cell mean is a sampling control, not a fourth alternative."
rk_models <- names(rk_labels)
rk_cells <- function(metric,rule="A-C",target=.8,period="2019-2026") vapply(rk_models,function(m)
 sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]",100*rk(metric,m,rule,target,period),100*rk(metric,m,rule,target,period,"low"),100*rk(metric,m,rule,target,period,"high")),"")
rk_changes <- vapply(rk_models,function(m) if(m %in% c("archived","random")) "—" else rdci("dives_avoided",model=m),"")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Ranking=unname(rk_labels[rk_models]),`Candidate sites selected (%)`=rk_cells("sites_selected","matched_high",.9),
 `Recorded dives avoided (%)`=rk_cells("dives_avoided","matched_high",.9),`Change in dive avoidance (points)`=rk_changes,check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

Upper habitat percentiles did not improve the habitat-only ranking: within reef-year AUC for useful dives was `r a3(rk("auc_useful","h_mean","habitat_only",0))` for the mean, `r a3(rk("auc_useful","h_q50","habitat_only",0))` for the median and `r a3(rk("auc_useful","h_q90","habitat_only",0))` for the 90th percentile. This does not rule out real habitat hotspots; it shows that favouring the best-valued part of a designated site did not improve this operational assessment.

No candidate met the pre-specified strong replacement gate: at least a one-point improvement in the primary recorded-dive trade-off, paired support against both controls, and gains sustained recently without loss of useful-dive retention. Recent CPUE had the best point estimates, so a separate experimental layer in `outputs/site_ranking_candidates/` is supplied for field comparison; the incumbent files and default selection are unchanged.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Appendix D: On-water workflow, density-aware classes and field trial {.unnumbered #sec-workflow-appendix}

The workflow was developed with GBRMPA in late October and early November 2026, after the original objectives were set, to translate the site ranking into decisions for a reef visit. It responds to GBRMPA's earlier ad hoc analysis of feeding-scar triggers. Scripts 33–37 (and 20b) produce every number below. The recommended settings, chosen after the 5 November 2026 delivery workshop, are density-aware v2 classes, a dive rule at A–D and a follow-up tow zone at A–C. Earlier settings are kept below because they show how that choice was reached. The workflow has not been trialled.

### Definitions {.unnumbered}

| Term | Definition used in the replay |
| --- | --- |
| Strong evidence | A tow recording at least one COTS, two or more counted feeding scars, or scars recorded as common in legacy surveys |
| Weak evidence | No COTS, and exactly one counted scar or scars recorded as present |
| Negative tow | No COTS and no feeding scars |
| Linked site | A designated site within 100 m of a tow's straight-line track |
| Open site | The last dive at the site in the previous 365 days exceeded 0.04 CPUE |
| Follow-up visit | A later visit to a reef already visited in the same season |
| Tow zone | A–C sites under the v2 classes, open sites and (with season memory) sites within 100 m of a strong tow on an earlier visit that season; a tow is in the zone if it passes within 100 m of a zone site |
| Dive rule | A dive without strong evidence nearby is made only at sites ranked A–D under the v2 classes at voyage departure |
| Density-aware classes | The same order of sites on each reef, with class shares that grow or shrink with the reef's expected density (below) |
| Density-aware v2 | Classes from each site's chance of a problematic dive, given the reef's recent density and the site's own record of dives and tows; reefs without recent evidence keep density quotas (below) |

: Definitions used in the workflow replay. {#tbl-workflow-definitions}

A dive whose only nearby strong tows were skipped by the zone counted as missed. Guiding tows were those on the reef from 30 days before a visit's first dive to its last dive, in recorded order; each tow belonged to the earliest visit whose window held it. Only runs of three or more consecutive tows outside the zone were skipped.

### Results under each setting {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-workflow-settings
#| tbl-cap: "Workflow settings under within-reef classes, replayed on 2019–2026 reef visits. Percentages are of all tows made, and of all ghost, low-density and above-0.04 dives under current practice; the mean CPUE has a 95% reef-year bootstrap interval. 'Ghost per miss' is ghost dives avoided per dive above 0.04 missed. The random row skips the same number of dives at random among those without strong evidence. COTS forgone remain available at the next visit."
wf_rows <- c("Site rule A–D, all dives" = SR, "Evidence rule: skip weak-scar dives" = "evidence rule: skip weak-scar dives",
             "Evidence rule: dive only on strong evidence" = "evidence rule: skip all non-strong dives",
             "Dive rule A–D" = "dive rule A-D", "Dive rule A–C" = WF, "Same number as A–C, at random" = RWF, "Dive rule A–B" = "dive rule A-B",
             "Tow zone, follow-up visits" = "zone only", "Tow zone with season memory" = "zone with season memory",
             "Dive rule A–C + follow-up tow zone" = WFZ)
has_ps <- function(v, m) any(pst$variant == v & pst$metric == m & pst$scope == "all visits")
cellp <- function(v, m) if (has_ps(v, m)) sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ps(v, m)) else "—"
cellci <- function(v, m, d = 3) if (has_ps(v, m)) sprintf("%s [%s–%s]", num(ps(v, m), d), num(ps(v, m, "low"), d), num(ps(v, m, "high"), d)) else "—"
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Setting = names(wf_rows),
  `Tows saved (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "tows_saved_pct"),
  `Dives skipped (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "dives_avoided_pct"),
  `Ghost avoided (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "ghost_avoided_pct"),
  `Low-density avoided (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "low_avoided_pct"),
  `>0.04 missed (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "high_missed_pct"),
  `Mean CPUE of missed >0.04` = vapply(wf_rows, cellci, "", m = "cpue_missed_high_mean"),
  `Ghost per miss` = vapply(wf_rows, function(v) if (has_ps(v, "ghost_per_high_missed")) num(ps(v, "ghost_per_high_missed"), 1) else "—", ""),
  `COTS forgone (%)` = vapply(wf_rows, cellp, "", m = "cots_forgone_pct"),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrlrr")
pzmd <- tab("protocol_zone_missed_dives.csv")
pzmd_lost <- as.logical(pzmd$memory_lost)
```

The dive-rule rows replay towing as it was recorded, so they save no tows. The zone acts on different dives, those that relied on a strong tow, so its effects add to the dive rule's rather than competing with it. In the last row, the zone's `r int(ps("zone with season memory", "high_missed"))` additional missed dives above 0.04 over eight seasons are the cost of skipping `r p0(ps(WFZ, "tows_saved_follow_up_pct"))` of follow-up tows. The replay counts all of them as missed; `r int(sum(pzmd_lost & pzmd$class %in% c("D", "E")))` of the `r int(sum(pzmd_lost))` were at sites ranked D or E, which the dive rule would not dive without strong evidence.

Among dives without strong evidence on 2020–2026 visits, those the recommended A–D rule would skip had a lower share above 0.04 (`r p1(cpf(TRUE, "high_share"))`) than those it kept (`r p1(cpf(FALSE, "high_share"))`), and a higher ghost share (`r p1(cpf(TRUE, "ghost_share"))` versus `r p1(cpf(FALSE, "ghost_share"))`). The trial decision rule below compares these two shares.

### Where ghost dives came from {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-workflow-pools
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded dives on 2019–2026 reef visits, by why the site could have been chosen. Weak-scar, negative and no-tow groups are classed by the strongest guiding tow within 100 m. AUC compares dives above 0.04 with ghost dives within visits, using the ranking at voyage departure."
pool_ids <- c("Open site" = "open", "Strong tow within 100 m" = "tow-triggered", "Weak-scar tow only" = "other: weak-scar tow",
              "Negative tows only" = "other: negative tows only", "No guiding tow within 100 m" = "other: no guiding tow")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Why the site was dived` = names(pool_ids),
  Dives = vapply(pool_ids, function(p) int(mzp(p, "dives")), ""),
  `Above 0.04 (%)` = vapply(pool_ids, function(p) sprintf("%.0f", 100 * mzp(p, "high") / mzp(p, "dives")), ""),
  `Ghost dives` = vapply(pool_ids, function(p) int(mzp(p, "ghost")), ""),
  `Ghost rate (%)` = vapply(pool_ids, function(p) sprintf("%.0f", 100 * mzp(p, "ghost") / mzp(p, "dives")), ""),
  `AUC, >0.04 vs ghost` = vapply(pool_ids, function(p) num(mzp(p, "auc_high_vs_ghost"), 2), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr")
```

Sites with no tow nearby were productive: skipping all of them would have lost `r int(ps("skip no-tow dives", "high_missed"))` dives above 0.04 to avoid `r int(ps("skip no-tow dives", "ghost_avoided"))` ghost dives. The dive rule therefore leaves them, like weak-evidence and negative-tow sites, to crew discretion within the permitted classes.

### The follow-up tow zone {.unnumbered}

Without season memory, the zone's `r int(ps("zone only", "high_missed"))` missed dives above 0.04 were concentrated: `r int(pzm$dives[1])` of them were at one site on `r sub(" [(].*", "", pzm$reef_name[1])` in `r pzm$year[1]`, holding `r p0(pzm$cots_share[1])` of the missed COTS, at CPUE up to `r num(pzm$max_cpue[1], 1)`. A strong tow on the season's first visit had flagged that site, but the ranking placed it in the lowest class. Keeping sites near earlier strong tows in the zone reduced the misses to `r int(ps("zone with season memory", "high_missed"))`. @fig-workflow-map shows the zone and recent tows on four reefs, under the density-aware v2 classes described below.

![Batt, Eyrie, Big Broadhurst and Lady Musgrave reefs under the proposed workflow. Cull sites are coloured by their 2027 density-aware v2 class ([density-aware v2](#sec-density-v2)); each panel gives the reef's expected share of problematic dives and its A, A–B, A–C and A–D site counts; the white dashed outline is the v2 follow-up tow zone (A–C sites plus 100 m), to which open sites and sites near earlier strong tows are added on the day. Dives without strong evidence are made only at A–D sites. Purple shading shows the exploration zones (darker is better-ranked habitat). Cyan lines are tows with strong evidence in the 12 months to 31 May 2026; light lines are other tows. Imagery: Esri World Imagery. The map illustrates the rules; it does not show measured performance on these reefs.](../outputs/figures/fig22_protocol_batt_eyrie.png){#fig-workflow-map width="100%"}

### Density-aware classes {.unnumbered #sec-density-classes}

The within-reef classes give every reef the same shares of sites: A 20%, A–B 50%, A–C 66% and A–D 80%. A reef with few COTS therefore has as many A sites as a reef in active irruption. The density-aware classes keep each reef's order of sites and change only how many of them reach each class. Script 20b calculates them in three steps.

First, a logistic model estimates the chance $p_{rj}$ that a dive at site $j$ on reef $r$ is problematic (CPUE ≥0.02):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{logit}\,p_{rj} &= \gamma_0+\gamma_1 h_{rj}+\gamma_2 D_r+\gamma_3\,\mathrm{logit}\frac{k_r+0.5}{n_r+1}+\gamma_4\log(1+n_r)\\
&\quad+\gamma_5 T_r+\gamma_6\,\mathrm{logit}\frac{m_r+0.5}{t_r+1}+\gamma_7\,\mathrm{logit}\,F_r .
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $h_{rj}$ is the site's percentile on its reef in the cull-site ranking. $n_r$ and $k_r$ are the reef's dives and problematic dives in the evidence window, and $t_r$ and $m_r$ its manta tows and strong-evidence tows; $D_r$ and $T_r$ indicate whether there were any. $F_r$ is the reef's irruption probability in the GBR-wide forecast for the previous year [@stewart2026hybrid].

Second, the reef's density $\bar p_r$ is the mean of $p_{rj}$ over its designated sites. Reefs with no dives or tows in the window are set by the forecast alone, discounted by the chance that such a reef needed culling at all; about one in five such reef-years had a problematic dive.

Third, the reef's class shares are shifted on the odds scale by its density relative to a typical culled reef:

$$
\delta_r=\mathrm{logit}\,\bar p_r-\mathrm{logit}\,\bar p_{\mathrm{typ}},\qquad
s_{rk}=\mathrm{logit}^{-1}\!\left(\mathrm{logit}\,b_k+\delta_r\right),
$$

where $b_k$ is the within-reef share for class $k$ or better (0.2, 0.5, 0.66, 0.8) and $\bar p_{\mathrm{typ}}$ is the median density over culled reef-years (`r num(sdk("typical_culled_reef_density"), 2)` for 2027). The site ranked $i$ of $n$ on its reef is in class $k$ or better when $(i-0.5)/n\le s_{rk}$. A typical reef keeps the within-reef shares.

For each test season, 2020–2026, the model, the unknown-reef discount and the typical density were refitted on earlier seasons only. In the cull-site selection test, at the same total number of sites as within-reef A–C, density-aware classes retained `r sdci("scaled", "ac_high_kept")` of dives above 0.04, against `r sdci("within", "ac_high_kept")`, but avoided fewer low-density dives at that budget (`r p1(sdv("scaled", "ac_low_avoided"))` against `r p1(sdv("within", "ac_low_avoided"))`). Only dived reefs could be scored, so the test says nothing about reefs never culled, where the forecast alone sets the classes.

### Density-aware v2 {.unnumbered #sec-density-v2}

Checks against reefs the program knows well showed two weaknesses in the first version. Big Broadhurst had `r int(v2rv("18-100a", "problematic_dives_12m"))` problematic dives out of `r int(v2rv("18-100a", "dives_12m"))` in the 12-month window, nearly all from the June–October 2025 voyages, and few since. The window counted them in full, giving a density of `r num(v2rv("18-100a", "reef_density_v1"), 2)`. John Brewer had `r int(v2rv("18-075", "dives_12m"))` dives, none problematic, and `r int(v2rv("18-075", "tows_12m"))` tows without a strong scar. It still scored `r num(v2rv("18-075", "reef_density_v1"), 2)`, because the model learned only from reef-years that crews chose to dive. Script 36 tested alternatives in the 2020–2026 replay. Script 37 writes the chosen one, density-aware v2, as a separate 2027 product.

*Reef density.* Each dive and tow in the year before planning is weighted by $0.5^{a/90}$, where $a$ is its age in days. The reef's density is the product of two logistic models with the reef terms of the first version. The first gives the chance that a survey occasion needs culling, meaning that a problematic dive follows. It is fitted on every cull-site reef's survey occasions, defined as dive and tow records split at gaps of more than 10 days, so tow-only surveys that found nothing count as zeros. The second gives the share of a cull visit's dives that were problematic. Ranked by this density, dives on 2020–2026 visits had a pooled AUC of `r num(dav("recent, two-part"), 3)`, against `r num(dav("density-aware"), 3)` for the first version. Half-lives of 60 to 180 days gave `r num(dav("sensitivity: half-life 60 d, two-part"), 3)`–`r num(dav("sensitivity: half-life 180 d, two-part"), 3)`; 90 days was set before the comparison. Without the irruption forecast, the results barely changed (@tbl-density-layers).

*Site classes.* On reefs with dives or tows in the past year, each site's score is the sum of two site-level log odds, the second at half weight:

$$
\mathrm{score}_{rj}=\mathrm{logit}\,p^{\mathrm{dive}}_{rj}+0.5\,\mathrm{logit}\,p^{\mathrm{visit}}_{rj}.
$$

Both models use the reef's log-odds density, the site's logit rank on its reef and the site's own record: dives at designated sites within 300 m and tows within 100 m, recent (90-day half-life within a year) and from one to six years before. $p^{\mathrm{dive}}$ is the chance that a dive at the site is problematic, fitted on dives. $p^{\mathrm{visit}}$ is the chance that the site received a problematic dive on a visit, fitted on every designated site of earlier visits, so it partly encodes where crews chose to dive. A site with no tow within 100 m in the past year is given the average recent strong-tow rate of the reef's towed sites. Without that rule, untowed lagoon patches outranked towed ground with strong scars, as on Tongue and John Brewer reefs. The A–B tow zone saved `r p1(pdv(V2, "A-B", "none", "tows_saved_follow_up_pct"))` of follow-up tows and missed `r int(pdv(V2, "A-B", "none", "high_missed"))` dives above 0.04 with the rule, against `r p1(pdv(V2A, "A-B", "none", "tows_saved_follow_up_pct"))` and `r int(pdv(V2A, "A-B", "none", "high_missed"))` without it; some untowed ground did hold aggregations. Class cut-offs are set on the training seasons' designated sites so that A, A–B, A–C and A–D hold 20, 50, 66 and 80% of them. Reefs without recent dives or tows keep the density quotas, using the v2 density, with sites ordered by the score.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-density-layers
#| tbl-cap: "Class layers compared at matched effort, 2020–2026 replay. Each layer's dive-rule and tow-zone results are interpolated to a common point. Ghost and low-density dives avoided are read where 3% of dives above 0.04 are missed. Dives above 0.04 missed are read where 14% of dives are skipped. Zone misses are dives above 0.04 lost where 12% of follow-up tows are saved. Brackets: 95% bootstrap interval over reef-years."
dl_rows <- c(`Within-reef` = "within-reef", `Density-aware v1 (12 months, dived reef-years)` = "density-aware",
             `Recent two-part density` = "recent, two-part", `Recent two-part, no forecast` = "recent, two-part, no forecast",
             `v2 before the untowed rule` = V2A, `Density-aware v2` = V2)
ci_txt <- function(l, m, scale = 100, d = 1) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", num(scale * dlmv(l, m), d), num(scale * dlmv(l, m, "low"), d),
                                                    num(scale * dlmv(l, m, "high"), d))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Layer = names(dl_rows),
                        `Ghost avoided (%)` = vapply(dl_rows, ci_txt, "", m = "ghost_avoided_at_3pct_missed"),
                        `Low-density avoided (%)` = vapply(dl_rows, ci_txt, "", m = "low_avoided_at_3pct_missed"),
                        `>0.04 missed (%)` = vapply(dl_rows, ci_txt, "", m = "high_missed_at_14pct_skipped", d = 2),
                        `Zone misses` = vapply(dl_rows, ci_txt, "", m = "zone_missed_at_12pct_tows_saved", scale = 1),
                        check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr")
```

Density-aware v2 was best on the two dive-rule measures. Paired with the first version, it avoided more ghost dives (`r dlmd(V2, "ghost_avoided_at_3pct_missed")`) and missed fewer dives above 0.04 (`r dlmd(V2, "high_missed_at_14pct_skipped")`), although the second interval just reaches zero. The weight of 0.5 was chosen on these test seasons from a grid of 0.5 to 5, so the margin is somewhat optimistic. Larger weights kept long-clean parts of dense reefs lower but missed more dives above 0.04 and lost tow-zone performance.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-density-workflow
#| tbl-cap: "The workflow under within-reef, density-aware (v1) and density-aware v2 classes, replayed on 2020–2026 reef visits. Zones include season memory; dive rules apply to dives without a strong tow within 100 m, with weak-scar, negative-only and no-tow sites left to crew discretion in the stated classes. Percentages are of follow-up tows and of all dives in each class under current practice. 'Ghost per miss' is ghost dives avoided per dive above 0.04 missed; @fig-ghost-per-miss shows the random baseline."
dw_rows <- data.frame(
  setting = c("Tow zone A–B", "Tow zone A–C", "Dive rule A–C", "Dive rule A–D", "Zone A–B + dive rule A–C", "Zone A–C + dive rule A–D"),
  zone = c("A-B", "A-C", "none", "none", "A-B", "A-C"),
  rule = c("none", "none", "A-C", "A-D", "A-C", "A-D"),
  evidence = c("none", "none", rep("discretion at A-x", 4)))
dw_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("within-reef", "density-aware", V2), function(ly) {
  v <- function(m) vapply(seq_len(nrow(dw_rows)), function(i) pdv(ly, dw_rows$zone[i], dw_rows$rule[i], m, evidence = dw_rows$evidence[i]), 0)
  gpm <- v("ghost_per_high_missed")
  data.frame(Classes = c("Within-reef", "Density-aware v1", "Density-aware v2")[match(ly, c("within-reef", "density-aware", V2))],
             Setting = dw_rows$setting,
             `Follow-up tows saved (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * v("tows_saved_follow_up_pct")),
             `Dives skipped (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * v("dives_avoided_pct")),
             `>0.04 missed` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", int(v("high_missed")), 100 * v("high_missed_pct")),
             `Ghost avoided (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * v("ghost_avoided_pct")),
             `Low-density avoided (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * v("low_avoided_pct")),
             `Ghost per miss` = ifelse(is.finite(gpm), num(gpm, 1), "—"),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(dw_tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrrrr")
```

The table covers `r int(pdtot$visits)` visits, `r int(pdtot$follow_up_visits)` of them follow-up visits. Reefs revisited within a season were usually denser than typical, so density-aware zones were larger on follow-up visits. These numbers cover 2020–2026 and differ slightly from the 2019–2026 replay above. Requiring at least a weak scar for every dive added misses almost as fast as at random, because dives at sites with no tow nearby were often productive. Density-aware v2 classes are stricter: the same cut-off skips more dives, which is why the dive rule moved to A–D under them.

@fig-ghost-per-miss compares ghost dives avoided per dive above 0.04 missed across the dive rules, the evidence-only rules and the random baseline. Rules that use evidence alone, such as diving only where tows found strong evidence, do no better than skipping dives at random. Every class-based rule does better than random, and v2 with the dive rule at A–D does best.

![Ghost dives avoided per dive above 0.04 missed, 2020–2026 replay. Grey: rules on tow evidence alone; light grey: the same number of dives skipped at random among dives without strong evidence; blue, orange and green: dive rules under within-reef, density-aware v1 and density-aware v2 classes, alone and with the follow-up tow zone. Whiskers: 95% interval over 300 reef-year resamples. Labels give the ratio and the dives above 0.04 missed; the three options with the highest ratio are outlined.](../outputs/figures/fig34_ghost_per_miss.png){#fig-ghost-per-miss width="100%"}

*Dense reefs.* On a dense reef, every version lifts most sites into A–C, including parts that tows have long found clean. Batt Reef's north-eastern flank is an example. It had `r int(bflv(V2, "tows_since_2019", "NE"))` tows since 2019, `r p1(bflv(V2, "strong_share", "NE"))` of them with a strong scar, against `r p1(bflv(V2, "strong_share", "SW"))` on the south-western flank. In 2027 it has `r int(bflv("within-reef", "a_to_c", "NE"))` of its `r int(bflv(V2, "sites", "NE"))` sites in A–C under the within-reef classes, `r int(bflv("density-aware", "a_to_c", "NE"))` under the first version and `r int(bflv(V2, "a_to_c", "NE"))` under v2; the site visit model alone gives `r int(bflv("two-part, site visit model", "a_to_c", "NE"))`. The replay does not support holding such ground down. On test visits to reefs denser than typical, `r int(dclv("site_visits"))` site-visits were at sites with at least five tows and no strong scar or dive in the previous one to six years. When crews dived them, `r p0(dclv("problematic"))` of `r int(dclv("dives"))` dives were problematic and `r int(dclv("high"))` were above 0.04. Long-clean tow records were a weak guide to the next season. This season's tows, through the tow zone and season memory, carry that information instead.

*2027.* The v2 product has `r int(v2cl("all reefs", "density_v2_a"))` A sites and `r int(v2cl("all reefs", "density_v2_a_to_c"))` A–C sites, against `r int(v2cl("all reefs", "density_v1_a_to_c"))` A–C under the first version and `r int(v2cl("all reefs", "within_a_to_c"))` within reefs. Big Broadhurst's density is `r num(v2rv("18-100a", "reef_density_v2"), 2)`, with `r int(v2rv("18-100a", "priority_a") + v2rv("18-100a", "priority_b") + v2rv("18-100a", "priority_c"))` A–C sites against `r int(v2rv("18-100a", "density_v1_a_to_c"))`. John Brewer's is `r num(v2rv("18-075", "reef_density_v2"), 2)`, with no A site and `r int(v2rv("18-075", "priority_b") + v2rv("18-075", "priority_c"))` B–C sites against `r int(v2rv("18-075", "density_v1_a_to_c"))` A–C. Reefs with tows but no dives in the past year have `r p0(v2cl("manta tows", "density_v2_a_to_c") / v2cl("manta tows", "sites"))` of sites in A–C. These rest on the site models; the replay can score them only where crews later dived.

### Field trial and monitoring {.unnumbered #sec-monitoring}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-workflow-voyage
#| tbl-cap: "What a voyage held, 2024–2026 seasons: median and 10th–90th percentile range. Tows are those made on the voyage; dives are at designated sites."
voy_rows <- c("Reefs visited" = "reefs", "Follow-up reefs" = "follow_up_reefs", "Manta tows" = "all_tows",
              "Tows on follow-up reefs" = "follow_up_tows", "Tows the v2 A–C zone with season memory would skip" = "tows_saved_memory",
              "Cull dives" = "dives", "Dives above 0.04" = "high", "Ghost dives" = "ghost",
              "Dives the v2 A–D rule would skip" = "flagged")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Per voyage` = names(voy_rows),
  Median = vapply(voy_rows, function(q) num(cpv(q), 0), ""),
  Range = vapply(voy_rows, function(q) sprintf("%s–%s", num(cpv(q, "p10"), 0), num(cpv(q, "p90"), 0)), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr")
```

A single voyage cannot test the dive rule. Resampling past voyages, the rule's skipped dives showed a lower share above 0.04 than its kept dives in `r p0(cpt(1))` of single voyages and `r p0(cpt(25))` of 25-voyage sets; `r p0(cpt(1, "p_none_flagged"))` of single voyages had no skipped dive at all. The proposed trial therefore has two parts:

1. **One live voyage** with at least three follow-up reefs. Freeze the ranking at departure. On follow-up reefs, tow the zone first and the rest of the reef afterwards, so ground is towed once and anything found only outside the zone is recorded. Flag dives the rule would skip and make them last, so their outcomes are kept. Record towing times, overrides and crew feedback. Proceed if the maps arrive before departure, crews can apply the rules without disrupting the schedule, the zone saves towing time and the rest of the reef finds no more dives above 0.04 than the replay suggests.
2. **A season of shadow recording.** Freeze the ranking before every voyage and change nothing on the water. After each voyage, score what the rule would have done from normal tow and dive records. Adopt the dive rule if, after about 25 voyages, skipped dives have a lower share above 0.04 and a higher ghost share than kept dives.

[TO CONFIRM: trial voyage, decision thresholds, monitoring owner and reporting route agreed with GBRMPA and vessel operators.]

The trial should compare outcomes with the search order crews would normally use. Its proposed adoption targets are a 10–15% reduction in designated sites requiring manta tows on individual visits and a 10–15% reduction in low-density or empty dives, with a negligible share of dives above 0.04 missed. Dives from 0.02 to 0.04 are reported separately. The retrospective reassessment does not establish both reductions at an agreed omission rate. [TO CONFIRM: the numerical tolerance for missed dives above 0.04 and whether reductions are measured per visit or over the full season.]

Sites deferred on one visit may be searched later, so initial site reductions cannot be read as annual time savings. Full-season effort must include annual full surveys, pre-closure and triggered checks, repeat dives and exploration visits. Annual full-coverage surveys and pre-closure checks offer chances to find missed populations, but their recovery rate has not been measured and later detections may be newly developed populations. Independent checks of a sample of deferred sites during the initial visit would help estimate the false-negative rate. Translating gains into vessel time or money requires an agreed account of travel, search, diving and culling time. [TO CONFIRM: whether to estimate financial savings and which operational cost data to use.]

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Appendix E: Larval dispersal and population modelling {.unnumbered #sec-connectivity-appendix}

### Hydrodynamic and particle transport model {.unnumbered}

A three-dimensional hydrodynamic model was developed using COMPAS–EMS to simulate circulation in the far northern Great Barrier Reef (FNGBR). The model domain extends from 14.254°S to 15.794°S and from 145.047°E to 145.766°E.

The model was nested within the 4 km resolution eReefs Great Barrier Reef hydrodynamic model (GBR4, version H4p0), which provided initial conditions and open-boundary forcing for currents, sea level, temperature and salinity, including tidal variability. Surface fluxes were calculated using atmospheric forcing from the Bureau of Meteorology Atmospheric high-resolution Regional Reanalysis for Australia (BARRA). Freshwater discharge and temperature inputs for two rivers were derived from a combination of the Queensland Department of Environment and Science Source catchment model and river gauge observations.

The model simulation covered 20 November 2022 to 1 April 2023, encompassing the COTS spawning period. The unstructured mesh was generated using JIGSAW [@engwirda2018primaldual], with spatially varying resolution to represent complex reef topography and narrow channels. The mesh comprised 45,756 cells, with horizontal resolution ranging from 160 to 1,300 m. Bathymetry was derived from the 30 m resolution dataset of @beaman2017gbr30.

Model performance was assessed against available observations of currents, sea level, temperature and salinity in the region. Observational datasets included:

- the Queensland Integrated Marine Observing System (IMOS) shelf-slope mooring east of Lizard Island, using temperature, salinity and current records from the GBRLSL-2209 and GBRLS-2303 deployments (AODN data catalogue);
- Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) temperature logger records (AIMS temperature data);
- EcoRAP temperature logger records.

Particle dispersal was simulated using COMPAS in transport mode. Particles were distributed across potential COTS habitat at a prescribed density per unit area. Each release comprised 2,519,724 particles, with releases occurring every two hours over a 24-hour period on 1, 7, 14, 21 and 28 December 2022 and on the same dates in January 2023. Particles were tracked for 45 days, with positions recorded hourly and saved in NetCDF format.

Daily mean larval concentrations were compared at ages 5, 9 and 10 days across the `r int(lc_scope$releases)` releases. Values were averaged by area to sub-reef sites and reefs, then ranked within releases. These ranks describe relative exposure, without identifying origins, settlement or source-to-destination connectivity.

Particle tracks were then used to estimate the strength of larval connections between reefs by simulating biological processes. We broadly followed the methodology of @stewart2026dispersal, in which ensemble modelling was applied to COTS larval dispersal. Here, however, we used a single biological parameterisation for computational reasons. We began by fitting functions describing age-dependent rates of survivorship and development to empirical COTS data [@pratchett2017larval], following @moneghetti2019kernels. These functions were then used to simulate many thousands of possibilities for each particle track, by allowing the simulated larva to settle at the first sub-reef it encountered while alive and competent. By comparing successful settlement events with the total number of simulated possibilities, and then aggregating across particle tracks, we estimated the strength of larval connections between all pairs of sub-reefs. These estimates form a network of larval connectivity, described by connectivity matrices. Each matrix contains elements $C_{i,j}(t)$, representing the probability that a larva released at sub-reef $i$ at time $t$ will survive and settle at sub-reef $j$.

### Larval settlement and concentration {.unnumbered}

As larval competency before 17 days was not measured, we assumed a minimum time to competency of 12 days post-fertilisation. The remaining fitted parameters of the survivorship and competency models are detailed in the Supplementary Materials of @stewart2026dispersal, and the model fits are shown in Figure 2 of that paper.

These functions were sampled repeatedly for each particle trajectory to produce a set of windows in which each simulated larva was both alive and competent, including samples that produced no such window. Where a window existed, the larva settled at the first sub-reef polygon it entered. Because sub-reef sites are small and clustered, no settlement radius was applied: larvae were considered settled only if they passed within a sub-reef site boundary, not within a given distance of it.

The concentration comparisons describe exposure, rather than source-to-destination exchange, at larval ages 5, 9 and 10 days across `r int(lc_scope$releases)` releases. Concentrations around Lizard varied among release dates, and elevated early-age concentrations in some releases did not consistently persist to later ages.

The broad north–south gradient makes an overall Lizard-versus-other-reefs contrast difficult to interpret. Comparing cross-shelf positions within latitude bands gives a more useful view (@fig-larval-cross-shelf). The central Ribbon Reefs generally ranked below nearby mid-shelf reefs at the later ages, whereas the southern Ribbon Reefs did not show the same pattern. Latitude bands reduce the influence of the broad gradient but do not remove all spatial dependence or possible boundary effects.

These results describe one spawning season. The local analysis plan calls for source-to-destination matrices for individual releases, explicit checks of sources and losses at the model boundary, and comparisons against connections based on distance alone. Those tests are needed before attributing concentration patterns to retention within reef groups, interpreting Ribbon Reef isolation, or using the patterns to identify reefs for source control. Exploratory reef-label permutations in the source analysis did not account for spatial autocorrelation; their p-values are not used here as confirmatory evidence. [TO CONFIRM: concentration units and source-buffer coverage with Sev and Owen.]

![Cross-shelf concentration ranks within latitude bands, with the northern band at the top. Each point is a reef, showing its mean within-release rank over the simulated releases; the horizontal line marks rank 0.5. Columns show larval age and colours identify shelf zones. This reformats source figure lc6. Broad latitude bands aid comparison but do not eliminate domain-boundary effects or spatial dependence.](../outputs/figures/fig30_larval_cross_shelf.png){#fig-larval-cross-shelf width="100%"}

### Population model and calibration {.unnumbered}

The strategic modelling strand extended COTSMod [@matthews2020cotsmod] through the Julia package COTSMod.jl, coupled to ADRIA and the CoralBlox coral model [@cotsmodmethods2026; @adriamethods2026; @dealmeida2026coralblox]. COTSMod.jl supplied population transitions, coral predation and larval processes; ADRIA supplied the spatial domain, disturbance forcing and scenario execution. The prototype used the Lizard Island cluster, with 2,895 sub-reef sites on 113 reefs. Historical simulations beginning in 1991 were assessed against AIMS Long-Term Monitoring Program (LTMP) manta COTS and coral records on Lizard Island, Eyrie, MacGillivray and North Direction reefs. The model state was expressed as recruit, juvenile and adult densities per hectare of site area, with coral cover represented relative to habitable area.

The working COTS formulation combines preferred-first per-capita grazing, survival linked to remembered preferred coral cover, adult senescence and preferred-food effects on reproductive condition. Larval production includes a low-density Allee effect, juvenile survival includes a saturating predator-pit term, and larvae are transported using reef-level connectivity and supplied from outside the domain. External supply is derived from the reef-level irruption-probability hindcast [@stewart2026hybrid]; its production multiplier is a calibration assumption, not measured recruitment. [TO CONFIRM: source and attribution of the annual 2018–2022 connectivity matrices.] Simulated adult density is converted to manta CPUE through a linear observation model, *CPUE* = *qA*, with *A* in adults ha$^{-1}$ and *q* = 0.015 COTS tow$^{-1}$ per adult ha$^{-1}$; nonlinear alternatives failed regional checks.

Since the earlier snapshot, the working model has incorporated revised coral thermal responses, a chlorophyll-based larval-survival modifier, wave-exposure effects on settlement, and revised initial population and coral settings. Initial fast-growing coral at Lizard Island was increased by 0.04 in absolute cover. Larger increases were rejected because they left too many COTS between irruptions. The linear observation conversion remains 0.015 COTS per tow per adult per hectare; nonlinear alternatives failed regional checks. These decisions improved the working calibration without identifying a unique population mechanism [@adriacalibrationreport2026].

The comparison comprises `r int(mcn("base_seeds"))` base seed pairs plus twelve one-at-a-time parameter perturbations of ±25%, giving `r int(mcn("calibration_arms_per_cull_state"))` runs in each culling state. Perturbations cover outside larval supply, background coral mortality, bleaching under low heat stress, the chlorophyll response, juvenile survival and initial fast-growing coral shares. Inner bands span the base seeds; outer bands span all runs. Neither is a probability interval, and joint parameter and structural uncertainty are not fully represented.

Recorded cull totals are now distributed among sites on the same reef in proportion to simulated population counts, retaining juvenile/adult stages and pre-/post-spawning timing. Removals remain limited by the animals available. This replaces the spatial-kernel allocation in the earlier diagnostic. Calibration scoring keeps culling off; paired culling-on runs provide the overlay. Earlier unmet-removal percentages therefore do not describe the current model.

The recent-density comparison (@fig-metacommunity-recent-density) shows partial agreement with diver estimates and differences among reefs. Corrected external irruption probabilities and density targets share cull and SALAD evidence, so this is a diagnostic comparison. 

![Recent adult COTS density with and without recorded culling, against SALAD diver estimates and catches converted to density (source Figure 2). The vertical axis is logarithmic. Lines are five-seed means; bands span seeds and parameter tests as in @fig-metacommunity-cots-coral. Larval-input corrections and density targets share observations, so agreement is not independent validation.](../outputs/figures/fig23_metacommunity_recent_density.png){#fig-metacommunity-recent-density width="100%"}

### Reefs outside the calibration score {.unnumbered}

Five monitoring reefs in the domain were reported but not used in the calibration score (@tbl-additional-reefs, @fig-metacommunity-additional). Martin and Linnet have irruption histories. Yonge, Carter and No Name have recorded at most 0.01 COTS per tow in 26–29 surveys since 1992. Ribbon No 10 has no monitoring series and is shown for comparison.

Martin and Linnet provide the more independent check, because the wave-exposure term does not act on them. The model's 1990s peaks fell in `r cpkv("Martin Reef", "1990s", "model_peak_year")` and `r cpkv("Linnet Reef", "1990s", "model_peak_year")`, against observed peaks in `r cpkv("Martin Reef", "1990s", "obs_peak_year")` and `r cpkv("Linnet Reef", "1990s", "obs_peak_year")`. Their 2010s peaks both fell in `r cpkv("Martin Reef", "2010s", "model_peak_year")`, against `r cpkv("Martin Reef", "2010s", "obs_peak_year")`. Heights were closer in the 1990s than the 2010s, when the model reached `r num(cpkv("Martin Reef", "2010s", "model_peak"), 2)` and `r num(cpkv("Linnet Reef", "2010s", "model_peak"), 2)` COTS per tow against `r num(cpkv("Martin Reef", "2010s", "obs_peak"), 2)` and `r num(cpkv("Linnet Reef", "2010s", "obs_peak"), 2)`. Against a no-model baseline, the mean observed series of the four calibration reefs, the model ordered survey years better but did not consistently identify irruption years better: on Martin it was worse at that, and on Linnet its mean absolute error was higher. Late-2026 surveys recorded 0.35 and 0.51 COTS per tow, above the model's 2026 values, in a reporting year beyond its end.

The three reefs with almost no COTS were first a failed check. Before the wave term, in preregistered runs of 19 October 2026, the model produced false irruptions on all three, with peaks of 0.33–0.48 COTS per tow and five to seven years at or above 0.22 under the linear observation model. Nothing in the model separated them from irruption reefs. Their most distinctive property was ocean-swell exposure, so a settlement multiplier was added on reefs with mean wave period above 6.6 s, falling to 0.25 at 7.0 s. Those limits were taken from monitoring records on 29 domain reefs that include these three. The term removed the false irruptions with almost no change to the calibration score, but agreement on these reefs is a check of its design rather than independent validation. Wave period also marks outer-shelf position, so the term cannot separate exposure from other outer-shelf properties such as low in-water chlorophyll.
<!-- 19 October pre-wave run: COTSMod-Calibration store/runs/20261019T_04_extra_reefs_w2_1991_v1
(extra_reefs_audit.csv), linear detection; wave rule and thresholds: docs/decision_record.md,
"Wave exposure: independent check" and "Preregistered: wave-exposure settlement mechanism".
Late-2026 surveys: same audit, obs_2027_cpue_late_2026_survey. -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-additional-reefs
#| tbl-cap: "Model against LTMP manta records, 1992–2026, on reefs outside the calibration score, for five-seed means without culling. The baseline is the mean observed series of the four calibration reefs, with no model. MAE is mean absolute error in COTS per tow. Spearman compares the ordering of survey years; it is undefined on No Name, which recorded no COTS. TSS is the true skill statistic for years at or above 0.22 COTS per tow, undefined where no such year was observed. The wave-exposure term was designed using the three reefs with almost no COTS."
ar_f <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.finite(x), num(x, d), "—")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Reef = car$reef,
  `Max COTS/tow, observed / model` = sprintf("%s / %s", ar_f(car$obs_max_cpue), ar_f(car$model_max_cpue)),
```

### Initial control projections to 2050 {.unnumbered}

The completed ensemble spans `r int(mcn("climate_models"))` climate models, five seed pairs, two climate pathways, nine culling levels and two treatments of the 2026 population state. The figures use the `r int(mcn("projection_arms"))` continuous-history runs without a population reset. Historical catches apply through 2026; effort-based culling begins in 2027. “Recent effort” uses 2023–25 diver-hours on each reef. Increased effort multiplies those hours; targeted effort reallocates the same total each half-year among reefs with at least 3 adults per hectare. Density-dependent catch rates determine adult removals, capped by the available population. Vessel travel and search costs are not represented explicitly.

Outside larval supply resamples historical irruption patterns and scales them by projected coral in the domain. These conditional scenarios include neither thermal acclimation nor external coral-larval supplementation. Excess simulated COTS in 2026 carry into the near-term projections. Proposed changes to the population reset, thermal acclimation scenarios and source-reef culling corrections had not yet entered the reported ensemble.

Increased effort lowered near-term COTS peaks, with climate-dependent coral outcomes. Reallocation could increase domain-wide removals without providing the largest benefit at the five displayed reefs (@fig-metacommunity-projection-effects). Population and coral summaries cover those reefs, whereas removals cover the whole domain. These summaries cannot establish domain-wide coral protection or an optimal allocation; local and downstream outcomes and operational constraints need further assessment.

The first three panels average Lizard Island, MacGillivray, North Direction, Eyrie and Martin; the last counts adult removals across the whole domain. “Recent” retains the recent allocation, “targeted” reallocates it, and multipliers scale total hours. ### Planned historical and fifth-wave assessments {.unnumbered}

The intended historical assessment pairs simulations with recorded removals from 2012 onward and simulations without program removals, starting from the same pre-control population and coral state and using matching environmental sequences and random seeds. Outcomes will include actual removals, infeasible requested removals, COTS abundance, larval export, cumulative coral consumption and coral cover. Holding external larval supply identical estimates the effect of control within the model domain conditional on unchanged outside reefs. A regional no-culling assessment instead requires an external supply history consistent with no control outside the domain. This experiment is a planned extension of the prescribed-removal diagnostics reported here; no completed paired program-impact estimate is asserted.

Future comparisons will examine stopping when local coral protection is no longer achievable versus continuing to reduce larval export, and when to begin or intensify control on reefs whose COTS populations cannot be reduced below a local target. Reallocation within existing vessel capacity and additional capacity will be compared separately, using current control and no control as references. Feasible removals must follow population availability and an effort–catchability relationship, rather than prescribed catches alone. Each paired comparison will share climate, disturbance and random-seed sequences, and repeat across plausible population, coral, connectivity and observation assumptions. Local and downstream coral outcomes and the resources required for fifth-wave suppression will be reported together. [TO CONFIRM: final effort–catchability model, projection horizon, vessel budgets, intervention rules and climate scenarios agreed with partners.]

### Limits of the population and dispersal results {.unnumbered}

The metacommunity results are calibration, diagnostic comparisons and exploratory projections within one northern reef cluster. Replicated runs and checks on reefs outside the calibration score improve the assessment but do not complete regional validation. Historical peak heights and between-irruption densities depend on the assumed relationship between manta observations and true abundance. Recent cull and SALAD observations helped construct corrected irruption inputs and also assess their fit. The current calibration uses five seed pairs and parameter sensitivity tests; projections additionally span five climate models. Those ranges do not capture all structural uncertainty. In particular, excess simulated COTS in 2026 carry into the near-term projections, outside larval supply is only approximately coupled to future coral, and thermal acclimation scenarios have not yet entered the reported ensemble. No estimate of historical program impact or future coral protection should be presented as validated until these assumptions and held-out performance have been assessed.

Larval connectivity has different roles in the two strands. It was not a predictor in the within-reef habitat ranking, whereas it carries population effects among reefs in the metacommunity model. The latter still uses reef-level transport and does not establish fine-scale transport among sites. Uncertainty in that transport, external larval pressure and coral disturbance must accompany any assessment of downstream control benefits.
